correctness.rationale: For fixed odd p, an exact cancellation gives p(b+1)=(p-a-1)q+1; b>=1 forces a in 1..p-2; modular inversion gives one coprime residue per a and uniquely determines b. The logarithm of the corresponding integer is ((p-a-1)/p) q log q+O_p(log q); monotone inversion yields cutoff (p/(p-a-1)) log X/loglog X. The fixed-modulus PNT in arithmetic progressions then yields p/((p-1)(p-a-1)) log X/(loglog X)^2 per class. Finite disjoint summation gives p H_(p-2)/(p-1). Exact regression factors and checks all n<=500000, and rational constants for 19 odd primes. The asymptotic itself is proved by PNT, not a finite experiment.
